Profile

More about me

I am a mechanical engineer, CFD engineer, and solver developer, currently working as a Research Associate and Doctoral Researcher at Technische Universität Clausthal. My core focus is computational fluid dynamics, multiphysics simulation, and numerical modelling, with experience in the analysis of complex fluid-flow and heat-transfer problems. My research experience includes OpenFOAM-based solver development, CFD–DEM coupling, multiphase and porous-media flows, and particle–fluid interaction modelling.

Beyond my doctoral research, my broader technical experience includes scientific programming, FEM simulation, HPC workflows, and engineering automation. I have also worked on parametric FEM studies at Fraunhofer IPMS and contributed to Formula Student chassis design—giving me a combination of research depth, practical engineering experience, and hands-on numerical modelling expertise.

What I do

Develop physics-based simulation tools

I modify and extend OpenFOAM solvers for CFD–DEM coupling, implement particle–fluid momentum exchange, improve MPI communication, and connect OpenFOAM with YADE for engineering-scale particle–fluid simulations.

01
How I work

Verify before I trust

I compare numerical results with analytical solutions, inspect transient and terminal behaviour, check conservation and force balance, and test sensitivity to time step, mesh resolution, software version, and parallel decomposition.

02
Technical range

From equations to scalable code

My workflow spans continuum mechanics, finite-volume discretisation, C++ solver development, Python automation, Linux, MPI, HPC execution, post-processing, and technical documentation in LaTeX.

03
Engineering mindset

Research with practical direction

My current doctoral research supports coupled simulation of rock boring and granular interaction. I am interested in roles where advanced simulation helps improve real products, processes, and engineering decisions.

04
My professional direction I am building toward a career in CFD, solver development, multiphysics simulation, and scientific computing—particularly in energy, aerospace, automotive, geomechanics, and other simulation-intensive industries.

Experience

Research Associate 09/2022 — Present
Technische Universität Clausthal · Clausthal-Zellerfeld, Germany
  • Developed and benchmarked OpenFOAM-based CFD solver extensions for incompressible, multiphase, porous-media, and particle–fluid interaction applications related to tunnel-boring-machine interaction with granular media.
  • Implemented C++/MPI-based coupling features for parallel data exchange, timestep synchronization, force coupling, volume-fraction coupling, and distributed particle search in coupled CFD simulations.
  • Validated solver accuracy against analytical and benchmark cases, achieving less than 1% terminal-velocity error in single-particle settling simulations.
  • Conducted cross-version benchmarking and parallel-consistency checks across OpenFOAM 10–14 to evaluate solver robustness, numerical accuracy, and scalability.
  • Improved coupled-solver stability by resolving timestep-control, force-exchange, volume-fraction, boundary-condition, and MPI communication issues during parallel runs.
  • Automated repetitive post-processing tasks using Python and C++, replacing manual data extraction with reproducible workflows for error analysis, trajectory tracking, and visualization.
  • Built validation workflows for single-particle settling and packed-bed pressure-drop cases against analytical and reference solutions.

Selected Research Output

Featured doctoral research

Coupled CFD–DEM Simulation of Particle–Fluid Systems Using OpenFOAM and YADE: Solver Development, Formulation and Verification

Development and verification of three OpenFOAM–YADE solvers—icoFoamYade, pisoFoamYade, and pimpleFoamYade—including rank-aware particle localization, Gaussian particle–mesh transfer, bounded volume-fraction mapping, semi-implicit momentum exchange, corrected buoyancy and torque treatment, and strengthened MPI communication.

Open Geomechanics manuscript · DOI pending
